text: AgenticSystemCore Summary An open format and a set of rules that turn a folder of Markdown into a wiki, a graph, an agent memory, a skills library, runnable architectures and a shared live board for agents and people, published here as a node of itself. Auto-wiki, distributed agentic memory, live specifications, evolving skills, runnable architectures and a self-driving live board — one open format for people and agents. Reference Node Level-0 of the Agentic Knowledge Web. AgenticSystemCore turns one folder of Markdown into a website, a knowledge graph and a local tool server for AI assistants at once — every link typed, every published artefact carrying a digest a reader can check, every change merged by a person or by a rule that person recorded — so people, search engines and AI agents read the same checked knowledge, with no server, database or language model needed to build, check or publish it. AgenticSystemCore is an open specification and reference implementation for knowledge that people and software agents can both read, verify and build on: a memory substrate that is deterministic, auditable, and governed by published conformance rules rather than by convention. text: Introduction Summary AgenticSystemCore turns a folder of Markdown files into a shared memory that people and software agents can both read, check, extend and run: a distributed brain whose meaning, form and rules are published, so any agent anywhere can use it, improve it and build systems from it. The idea Most knowledge that agents use today lives in one of two places: inside a single vendor's memory service, or scattered across documents that no machine can verify. text: Reading the specification Summary A key to the specification's notation: what the rule identifiers mean, how the key words MUST and SHOULD are used, what the small bracketed references at the end of each rule are, why some rules are marked reserved, and how error codes, vectors and Levels fit together. The specification is exact so that two implementers in two languages produce the same bytes. That exactness makes it dense. This page explains its conventions, so that the rule text can be read for what it says. Sections and rules The specification has twelve sections, AGSC-00 to AGSC-11 , each a page under /specs/ ; a section too long for one page is published in numbered parts, each with the section's title and a part line, and a link to a rule always names the part that carries it. Every rule has a stable identifier of the form AGSC-<section>-<number> , for example AGSC-03-01 , which is the first rule of the links section. Identifiers are never reused or renumbered ( AGSC-00-16 ). On this site every identifier is a link: click one to reach the rule, and copy the address to cite it. The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY are used as defined in BCP
title: Reading the specification

text: AGSC-00 — Overview, terms, conformance model Summary What the specification covers, the words it uses, what it means to conform, and how versions change. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.6 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-29. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no standards body has reviewed or adopted it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language What it is. AgenticSystemCore is a file format plus a few fixed outputs. You write knowledge as Markdown files with a small YAML header, keep them in one directory with one configuration file, and a conforming tool turns that directory into a website, a graph, a search index, an agent-facing text file, a chunk export and a discovery document — the same bytes every time, on any machine. What conformance means. A tool is a reader , a writer or a full engine ; a published site is a node at Level 0 to 3. A claim names the class or Level, the spec_version and the test vectors passed. There is no badge and no registry — the vectors are the proof. Terms you will meet. A Bundle is the directory. An Item is one file;

text: AGSC-02 — Item: frontmatter contract per type Summary One Markdown file with a small YAML header: the keys every item has, what each of the six types adds, the body rules, and the ports, architectures, attachments and task states. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.6 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-29. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no standards body has reviewed or adopted it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language One file. An item is a Markdown file that starts with a YAML block between --- lines. The YAML is a small, safe subset: no anchors, no aliases, no custom tags. Common keys. type , title , description , tags , clusters , status , date , modified , sources , verified , prov (who or what made it), and the typed link keys. Lengths are counted in Unicode code points. Six types. Concept (with a kind : pattern, taxonomy, explainer, principle, decision, spec, task, term, or a saved architecture ), Episode (something that happened), Procedure (steps a reader can run; exports as a skill), Lesson (distilled from episodes, with a severity), Clus
title: AGSC-02 — Item: frontmatter contract per type

text: AGSC-04 — Canonicalization and determinism Summary Why two builds anywhere give the same bytes: canonical JSON, NFC text, one time format, fixed sort orders and SHA-256. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.6 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-29. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no standards body has reviewed or adopted it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language The promise. Time is one instant format in UTC, taken from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH or the last commit. Every list has a stated sort order. Hashes are SHA-256, lowercase hex. Unicode. text: AGSC-05 — Graph: IRIs, RDF views, SKOS, PROV Summary How items become a graph with web addresses, the three RDF views, the ontology and its alignment to SKOS, PROV-O and Dublin Core, and the byte-level pins. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.6 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-29. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no standards body has reviewed or adopted it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language Every item is a node with a web address ( <site>/concepts/<slug>/ ), and every link is an edge. The Bundle is exported as JSON-LD, Turtle and N-Quads — one graph, three syntaxes — plus one file per item; those are the four RDF views, and RDF/XML is not emitted at 1.x ( AGSC-05-06 ). The vocabulary. A small OWL 2 RL ontology ( ontology/agsc.ttl , CC0) with 12 classes and 40 properties, aligned to SKOS (concepts and clusters), PROV-O (episodes, procedures, gates, reviews, sources) and Dublin Core. There is deliberately no common Item class. No inference at build. Everything a consumer might expect from reasoning — inverses, cluster nesting — is written out e

text: AGSC-11 — The node boundary: cross-origin access, federation, contribution, surfaces, visibility, retirement Summary Where a node meets the outside: cross-origin access, the nine parts of federation, the plugin contract for every agent surface, visibility, retirement and tombstones. Status of this document Specification 1.0.0-rc.6 , a release candidate tagged on 2026-09-29. It is an independent specification: it is not a standard of the IETF, the W3C or any other body, and no standards body has reviewed or adopted it. Released sections are immutable; a correction ships as a new version. In plain language Where it applies. Every place a node meets something outside itself: a browser reading across origins, another node, a URL somebody else typed, a reader who may not be allowed to see everything. All of it is static and client-side — nodes never call nodes. Parameters. Every number and every list in this chapter lives in the configuration file with a default and a maximum; a reader that meets a value it does not know treats it as the most restrictive one and never fails. Cross-origin. Public artefacts are readable from any origin; a restricted node still publishes its discovery file

text: MCP knowledge extension Summary The reference text of the MCP extension identifier com.agenticsystemcore/knowledge: what a server says by declaring it, how it declares it, the seven tools and the security floor they inherit. The identifier com.agenticsystemcore/knowledge names an unofficial extension of the Model Context Protocol. A server that serves a Bundle over MCP declares it to say that the same knowledge is also published as static files, and where the discovery document for those files is. This page is that extension's reference text. It is also the documentation route that a node declaring the mcp surface points at ( AGSC-11-16 ). Status Extension identifier com.agenticsystemcore/knowledge Protocol revision Model Context Protocol 2026-07-28 Standing An unofficial extension under MCP SEP-2133, which says that "Unofficial extensions are not recognized by MCP governance and may be introduced and governed by developers outside the MCP organization". It needs no permission and has no registry entry, and it has not been submitted as an MCP SEP. Specification 1.0.0-rc.6 , a release candidate.
